paragraphs: Rav Papa, son of Rav Nachman.
Mentioned in Bava Metzia 113a, explaining before Rav Yosef; but Dikdukei Soferim reads R' Papa, son of Rav Channin.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: דק״ס is conventionally Dikdukei Soferim, without freshly checking an edition or importing its author’s identity. The stated variant changes the father Nachman to Channin, without merging canonical persons.
קיג. gives 113a under the period convention. תרגם is active offered an explanation before Yosef, not passive translation of a missing Aramaic phrase; teacher is not separately stated.

נזכר and the following explaining naturally refer to the headed Papa. The heading’s two full רב titles, Yosef’s and Channin’s full titles remain Rav. The variant prints ר״פ; Papa is a contextual name expansion, while its title remains R' and does not inherit the heading’s Rav.
